headline: White House: Trump + AI CEOs ink “morally binding” voluntary safety accord (internal controls, independent audits, board oversight); OpenAI ships always-on Dots agents on GPT-6 Astra; US completes Iraq troop exit.

stories.title: Trump + AI CEOs sign voluntary “morally binding” safety accord
facts: White House lunch Tue (~2h): Trump posted a voluntary accord on Truth Social that he called “morally binding” / “almost like a constitution” — no legal force, opens door to later codification.

Signers on the posted document (Euronews/CNN): Trump, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, Google’s Sundar Pichai, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI’s Greg Brockman, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Elon Musk (X/SpaceX/xAI).

Four voluntary steps (Bloomberg/CNN): robust internal controls (cyber/bio/chem/unintended acts); internal monitoring team; independent external auditor; board committee on audit reports — plus regular best-practice meetings.
Trump said he’ll name ~10 people to “watch over the whole enterprise” and someone to oversee the deal soon; still rejects slowing AI vs China — also floated renaming AI to “super intelligence.”
Context: pressure after OpenAI/Anthropic agent-safety headlines; Amodei told reporters the tech has “very real risks” and how to address them is “still under discussion.”
stories.whyItMatters: Overnight’s political answer to the week’s agent-safety scare is voluntary self-policing — audits and board committees without new liability rules.

stories.title: OpenAI ships Dots — always-on agents on GPT-6 Astra
facts: OpenAI (Sep 29 / DevDay): Dots are proactive, always-on agents with their own cloud computer + browser; connect to 4,000+ apps via plugins; reachable in ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams.
Powered by GPT-6 Astra (despite GPT-6.1 Astra being held). Rollout: Pro + Business Premium in eligible markets today (first Dot included); Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare beta when workspace admin enables.
Safety pitch: background “proactive research” uses read-only tools; saved passwords used without exposing them to the model; auto-review + Custom Rules for approvals; monitoring can pause/stop a Dot.
Specialist org Dots (own identity/credentials) in focused enterprise pilots; Microsoft Agent 365 integration planned. HN: ~534 pts overnight.
stories.whyItMatters: Same DevDay week as Sol pricing news — OpenAI is shipping a consumer/enterprise always-on agent product while still pausing tool-use on its most capable training runs.

stories.title: US completes withdrawal from remaining Iraq bases
facts: AP / Reuters (Baghdad, Wed): US forces withdraw from remaining bases in Iraq today — exit agreed 2024 under Biden, carried out under Trump even amid conflict with Iran.
Tehran/allies cast it as a win for the “axis of resistance”; Iraqi analysts warn of a security vacuum for Iranian-backed militias and Islamic State sleeper cells.
US troops had supplied intel/ISR against IS; ~4,500 US dead over 20+ years; 7 of 18 US service members listed killed in this year’s Iran conflict were in Iraq.
stories.whyItMatters: End of the post-2014 US advisory footprint in Iraq — timed while Washington is still in a wider fight with Iran.

stories.title: Germany: Pflege reform still unresolved for Kabinett; Reiche orders more gas into storage
facts: Deutschlandfunk: ahead of today’s planned Kabinett decision on the Pflegereform, Union and SPD still not aligned — SPD (Miersch) keeps demanding changes beyond a pure cuts package.

Handelsblatt/dpa overnight: talks ran through Tuesday; Linnemann draft aims to avoid next-year contribution hikes (e.g. stretching Pflegeheim Leistungszuschläge — ~€2.6B 2027 relief in Warken-era draft).
Handelsblatt (ministry circles): Wirtschaftministerin Reiche instructed state gas trader Sefe late Tue (aligned with Merz) to store more gas — fill level ~57% vs ~70% typical this time of year.
stories.whyItMatters: Two overnight domestic pressure points: care-insurance politics before Kabinett, and a harder winter gas-storage push.
